chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan reported to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon them both) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

There is no step more beloved to God than two steps: a step by which a believer fills a rank in the way of God, and a step by which a believer goes to a kinsman who has severed ties, to reconnect them.
And there is no swallow more beloved to God than two swallows: a swallow of anger that a believer repels with forbearance, and a swallow of grief that a believer repels with patience.
And there is no drop more beloved to God than two drops: a drop of blood in the way of God, and a drop of tears in the darkness of the night out of fear of God.

key_terms.جرعة: Swallow/gulp — metaphor for enduring something bitter (anger or grief)
key_terms.خشية الله: Fear/awe of God — reverential consciousness that leads to tears in worship
key_terms.خطوة: Step — metaphor for a purposeful action taken in obedience to God
key_terms.سبيل الله: The way of God — striving and sacrifice for God’s cause
key_terms.قطرة: Drop — metaphor for a precious small sacrifice (blood or tears)

ai.seo_question: What are the most beloved deeds to God according to Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), through a chain traced to Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS), highlights three categories of deeds most beloved to God, using vivid physical metaphors: steps (striving in God’s path and mending family ties), swallows (controlling anger with forbearance and bearing grief with patience), and drops (blood shed for God’s cause and tears shed in nocturnal devotion). This tripartite structure was a common Prophetic teaching style that made ethical guidance memorable for the early Muslim community.
